title: How the SDKs call the PAC file endpoints: clone, validate and version actions

prose.text: These are claims about how the Python and Go SDKs call the PAC file endpoints, not about PAC behavior in the service. The product model is in [[zia.traffic-forwarding.pac]].

prose.label: Version actions.

get-returns-all-versions.statement: `get_pac_file` reads `/pacFiles/{id}/version`, and its docstring says it retrieves all versions of a PAC file for the ID; `get_pac_file_version` reads one version.

clone-strict-signature.statement: `clone_pac_file` has fixed arguments rather than `**kwargs`. The SDK's docstring says the clone endpoint takes only version-level fields, and that sending parent fields such as name or domain, or `pacVersion`, in the body makes the API answer 400 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND instead of an input error.

quotes: Sending parent-level fields (name/description/domain/...) or the path parameter ``pacVersion`` in the body causes the API to reject the request with a misleading 400 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND

clone-needs-committed-parent.statement: The SDK's docstring says the clone request must be made against committed state: a parent created in the same session must be activated first, or the clone fails with the same 400 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

validate-raw-body.statement: `validate_pac_file` sends the PAC source as the raw request body, dedented and stripped of leading line breaks, and the request executor special-cases `/pacFiles/validate` so the body goes out as data without JSON conversion.

quotes: def validate_pac_file(self, pac_file_content: str) -> APIResult[dict]:
# Send the PAC content as raw data
pac = textwrap.dedent(pac_file_content).lstrip("\r\n")
body=pac,
# For PAC file validation, send as raw data without any modification
if "/pacFiles/validate" in endpoint and service_type == "zia":
# For PAC file validation, send as raw data without any modification request["data"] = body

python-action-body-is-object.statement: Python's `update_pac_file` puts the action in the path and sends the remaining keyword arguments, including `pac_commit_message`, as a dictionary body that the executor sends as JSON.

json_payload = self._prepare_body(endpoint, body)
request["json"] = json_payload

go-action-body-is-raw-commit-message.statement: Go's `UpdatePacFile` takes a `commitMessage` string and, when it is not empty, sends it as the raw request body. Its doc comment says the endpoint expects the commit message as the raw request body (not a JSON object) and that sending a serialized object corrupts the version's stored commit message.

automate-action-operation.statement: The Automate OpenAPI capture lists the PAC version action as the operation 'Pac Resource Update Pac Version Flag' with path parameters and an optional newLKGVer query parameter, and the operation carries no requestBody member.

expect.operationId: Pac Resource Update Pac Version Flag

action-body-contract.title: What the PAC version-action endpoint accepts as a request body
action-body-contract.blocks: saying whether the Python object body or the Go raw commit message is the correct write, and what commit message ends up stored
action-body-contract.detail: Unverified legacy statement: do not infer that the Python call fails without a live request trace. Run the version action from each SDK against a scratch PAC file and read the stored commit message back.
